definitions.explanation: Having the form or pattern of waves; used to describe shapes, patterns, or phenomena that come in successive waves.

examples.japanese: {波状|はじょう}の{模様|もよう}が{美|うつく}しい。
{波状|はじょう}{攻撃|こうげき}が{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: Wave after wave of attacks continued.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{波状|はじょう}の{揺|ゆ}れが{何度|なんど}も{繰|く}り{返|かえ}された。
examples.english: After the earthquake, undulating tremors repeated many times.

notes:
A compound of {波|は} (wave) and {状|じょう} (shape/form). Used both literally for physical wave-like shapes and figuratively for things that come in successive waves. The suffix {状|じょう} is productive and creates adjective-like nouns describing shape: {球状|きゅうじょう} (spherical), {帯状|おびじょう} (belt-shaped), {環状|かんじょう} (ring-shaped).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波状|はじょう}{攻撃|こうげき}: wave attack; successive attacks in waves
- {波状|はじょう}の{模様|もよう}: wavy pattern
- {波状|はじょう}{雲|うん}: undulating clouds

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {波形|はけい}: waveform (more technical, referring to the shape of a signal or wave)
- {波打|なみう}つ: to undulate; to ripple (verb form)
- うねり: swell; undulation (more colloquial)
